proposals.before: In the eighth month of autumn Zhu Yougui sent Han Gong, Kang Huaiying, and Niu Cunjie with fifty thousand men in a furious siege of Hezhong.
proposals.after: In the eighth month of autumn Zhu Yougui sent Han, Kang Huaiying, and Niu Cunjie with fifty thousand men in a furious siege of Hezhong.
proposals.reason: Chinese has only the surname 韓 with no given name; idiomatic invents the given name Gong.

proposals.before: That same day eleven Yan officers led by Situ Quanshuang defected with their families.
proposals.after: That same day eleven Yan officers led by Si Quanshuang defected with their families.
proposals.reason: Chinese surname is 司 (Si), not the compound Situ; idiomatic over-translates the surname.

proposals.before: Yang Shihou held the east bank of the Zhang; Cunxu camped at Zhanggong Bridge until staff officer Cao Jinjing went over to Liang; the Jin host faltered and pulled back.
proposals.after: Yang Shihou held the east bank of the Zhang; Cunxu camped at Zhanggong Bridge until staff officer Cao Jinjin went over to Liang; the Jin host faltered and pulled back.
proposals.reason: Chinese 曹進金 is Cao Jinjin; idiomatic adds a medial 'g' as Jinjing.

proposals.before: Yang Shihou had just died at Weizhou; the Liang Founder split Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate circuit, made Delun commissioner of Weibo and Zhang Jun commissioner of Xiang, and the Wei troops refused to submit.
proposals.after: Yang Shihou had just died at Weizhou; the Liang ruler split Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate circuit, made Delun commissioner of Weibo and Zhang Jun commissioner of Xiang, and the Wei troops refused to submit.
proposals.reason: Chinese 梁主 here is the reigning Liang emperor (Zhu Youzhen), not the deceased Liang Founder; idiomatic over-specifies Founder.

proposals.before: That month the Liang Founder sent Wang Tan with fifty thousand from Yindi Pass to storm Taiyuan; Li Sizhao sent Shi Jiacai with three hundred horse.
proposals.after: That month the Liang ruler sent Wang Tan with fifty thousand from Yindi Pass to storm Taiyuan; Li Sizhao sent Shi Jiacai with three hundred horse.
proposals.reason: Chinese 梁主 is the reigning Liang emperor, not the deceased Founder.

decisions.after: In the eighth month of autumn Zhu Yougui sent Han Qing, Kang Huaiying, and Niu Cunjie with fifty thousand men in a furious siege of Hezhong.
decisions.reason: The chapter's 韓、 is a damaged or truncated reading. Parallel passages identify Zhu Yougui's general as Han Qing (韓勍), so neither invented 'Han Gong' nor the bare surname is adequate.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 友珪……見統軍韓勍；韓勍為友珪謀

decisions.reason: 司 is the surname Si; it is not the compound surname 司徒.
曹進金 romanizes as Cao Jinjin, not Cao Jinjing.
After Zhu Yougui's death, 梁主 denotes the reigning Later Liang ruler Zhu Youzhen, not the dynasty's founder.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 友珪僭即帝位……梁主乃割相、衛、澶三州

decisions.reason: 梁主 again denotes the current Later Liang ruler; the Founder had already been murdered in s0031.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 梁祖為其子友珪所弑……梁主遣別將王檀

claimRetractions.reason: Han Gong is an unsupported name created from the mistranslation.
Situ Quanshuang is a duplicate bad name generated from the mistranslated surname.

claimRevisions.reason: The parallel tradition restores the general's full name as Han Qing (韓勍).
The English name claim must match the corrected romanization Cao Jinjin.
The title claim must remain neutral because this is the reigning Liang ruler, not the founder.
The title claim must match the corrected neutral rendering for the reigning Liang ruler.
